what: an input -ss into MPEG-TS (.ts, .m2ts, .mts) or MPEG-PS (.mpg) lands inside a GOP, because those demuxers seek by timestamp onto any packet and not back to a keyframe, and nothing decodes before the next keyframe: look.py --at, --compare and the contact sheet on a TS with one keyframe wrote nothing (kind output, 'sweep_look.png: not written'); with a keyframe every 2 s look.py --at 3 showed the frame at 4 s; cut.py --accurate wrote no picture (verified false) or started on another frame with verified true; the review page's stills were missing; cropdetect.py --motion-centre measured 3 of 15 readings without saying so
escaped: the TS fixtures of the contact-sheet and cut tests have a keyframe every 15 frames, so a seek always had a keyframe close behind it; SEEK_MARGIN (1 s) was sized for the MP4 B-frame reorder delay, and the frame grabs (look, the review page, cropdetect, fit's crop check, scenes --shots) seeked with no margin at all; tests/sweep.py compares what tools said, and the analysis tools skip an empty window silently
mechanism: decision.seek_margin(meta, t) is the one rule for how far before a time an input seek starts (10 s on the mpegts and mpeg demuxers, SEEK_MARGIN elsewhere); cut.py, sync.py and fit.py's trim use it in place of SEEK_MARGIN, look.py drops it with trim or a select on the file's clock, and probe.seek_args gives the analysis decodes, and _review.still the review page stills, the same margin on those demuxers; TimestampSeekTests runs look (--at at two times, --compare, the sheet) and cut --accurate on .ts, .m2ts, .mts and .mpg fixtures with one keyframe, and an MP4 control, comparing the frame written with the frame decoded from the start
